ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory customer due diligence screening against the PEP designation as defined in the Cyprus AML Law and FATF Recommendations; continuous screening against OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, and the Cyprus National Sanctions List; enhanced due diligence and source-of-wealth verification for all PEPs and high-risk jurisdictions; screening must be performed before appointment, with results documented and retained for at least five years post-termination.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRCOR) e-Filing Portal — https://efiling.companies.gov.cy
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be submitted in Latin script; Greek names must be transliterated into Latin characters for the electronic register. In bilingual practice, the Greek version may also be used on a Greek-language certificate but the DRCOR record is Latin-script based. The name must end with 'Limited' or 'Ltd' (or Greek equivalent as accepted by DRCOR) and must not contain misleading or offensive expressions. Only registration-standard characters, spaces, and Arabic numerals are permitted; special symbols and punctuation are restricted.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the DRCOR rejects a name, the applicant may submit a written appeal through the e-Filing portal within 30 days of refusal, attaching evidence of distinguishing features and any required ministerial approval for sensitive words. The appeal is considered by the Registrar's legal unit. If rejected again within 30 days, the applicant may initiate an administrative recourse before the Cyprus Administrative Court under Article 146 of the Constitution within 75 days of notification. An alternative course is to immediately file a modified name application, preserving the existing reservation if still valid.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is accepted for low-risk PropTech SaaS companies where a physical address in Cyprus is designated for statutory service of process and official correspondence. The DRCOR does not require staff presence at the registered address, but the address must not be a PO Box. A virtual office provider with physical mail handling and scan-forward services is compliant for ISIC 6201 and no statutory license governs this activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low_Moderate_Risk (estimated 5% likelihood of an unannounced DRCOR or Cyprus Police AML/Cyber inspection in the first year, with probability rising to ~10-15% only if sanctioned transactions, PEP exposure, or adverse media triggers enhanced AML monitoring; tax audit inspection is more likely document-based with inspection probability ~8%).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law, Cap. 113 (as amended), particularly ss. 3, 5, 6, 10, 17, 20 and Schedule 1 (Table A)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRCO), Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry, Nicosia, Republic of Cyprus
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association (Kαταστατικό) lodged with the Registrar; Certificate of Incorporation issued thereafter
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None – Cyprus private limited companies may be incorporated with any nominal share capital (commonly EUR 1,000 divided into EUR 1 shares); no minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement for general PropTech SaaS activities.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the initial subscribers' share subscriptions to the company's share capital, as recorded in the register of members, be and are hereby approved and allotted. RESOLVED that the registered office of the company be and is hereby established at the address registered with the Registrar of Companies in the Republic of Cyprus. RESOLVED that [Name, Passport/ID No. ________] be and is hereby appointed first director, and [Name, Passport/ID No. ________] be and is hereby appointed first secretary. RESOLVED that the directors are authorized to execute all filings, pay all fees and open the corporate bank account. RESOLVED that the director's qualification be fixed at one share. RESOLVED FURTHER that the company adopt its common seal in digital form.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRCO) – Companies Section, Nicosia (online via Cyprus e-Registry / BizFeed portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three proposed company names through the DRCO online name reservation service (or via a licensed legal agent). Reserve the names to prevent duplication; the name must end with 'Ltd' or 'Limited' and not be identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered name. Pay the name reservation fee and await certificate of name approval.
required_dossiers: Application for name reservation (Form HE-Name Appeal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected because of similarity or prohibited words, file a name appeal with DRCO within 15 days, or submit an alternative name; an incorrect refusal due to similarity can be cured by written submission of existing registrations and consent letter from the existing company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Subscribers, notary public and licensed lawyer (authorized to witness signatures)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English or Greek, compliant with Cap. 113. Each subscriber signs the Memorandum in the presence of a witness (or notary). The Articles must include the company's name, registered office clause, share capital clause, and directors' powers. Have the signature pages notarized and obtain the notary's certificate for registration.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (original signed)
Consent of each named director/secretary to act (Form HE1?)
Statement of compliance under s. 10 of Cap. 113
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar returns documents for deficiency, rectify the non-compliant clauses, re-execute before a notary and re-submit within 30 days; the notary's certificate should be corrected if it contains inaccurate personal data.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRCO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the executed Memorandum and Articles, Form HE1 (statutory declaration of compliance), Form HE4 (notice of directors and secretary), and notice of registered office with the DRCO. Registration can be made electronically through the e-Companies portal or physically at the Nicosia office. Pay the incorporation fee and gazette publication fee. Upon internal review, the Registrar will incorporate the company and issue a Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Passport copies and proof of address for all officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query or rejection, address the query in writing within 15 days, provide corrected forms, or withdraw and re-file; judicial review before the administrative court remains available for unlawful refusals.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRCO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful registration, obtain the Certificate of Incorporation (Entry into the Register). Verify the company's name, registration number, date of incorporation and registered office. The certificate is conclusive evidence that the company is authorized to commence its business.
required_dossiers: Previous filing documents (if not already uploaded)
Identity of applicant/agent to collect or receive digital certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains clerical errors, apply for rectification under Cap. 113; if the certificate is not issued within SLA, escalate to the DRCO senior management or apply to the District Court for a mandamus order.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Board, Registered Agent, Tax Department and Social Insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting and pass the board resolution approving share subscription, registered office, and officer appointments as provided. Prepare statutory registers (members, directors, secretaries, charges). Register for the 12.5% Cyprus corporate income tax, the VAT (0% software services may be zero-rated or subject to reverse charge), and complete data protection registration under GDPR if the SaaS processes EU personal data. Open a corporate bank account and, if hiring, register employers with the Social Insurance Services.
required_dossiers: Statutory registers (Register of Members, Directors, Secretaries)
Application for Tax Identification Number (TIC) / VAT registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax or bank approval is delayed, provide clarification letters, update the agent's KYC documents, or escalate via the Tax Department's taxpayer service; any incorrect data in statutory registers must be amended by board resolution and filed as a Form HE4 change from the original registration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no industrial licensing board triggered by the PropTech SaaS scope (ISIC 6201); physical industrial permitting only applies to manufacturing/factory activities under the Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no operational or manufacturing license is required for a cloud-based real estate management SaaS; the Certificate of Incorporation, tax registration, and general labor/digital permits are sufficient.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environment, Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Environment (Republic of Cyprus)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – the activity is a purely digital software platform; no EIA screening or registration is required because there is no physical construction, industrial plant, land disturbance, or waste generation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable – the company does not generate regulated wastewater, Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs), or solid/hazardous waste. General office waste is managed under municipal collection regulations; any rented office must comply with the Cyprus 'Law on Waste' (185(I)/2011) for waste classification, but no specific discharge permits are required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office workplace must be cleared by the Labour Inspection Department (Ministry of Labour, Welfare and Social Insurance) on first use. Fire safety in office premises is evidenced by a Fire Service clearance (Civil Defence Act) issued by the Cyprus Fire Service for premises with more than 20 employees; the company must ensure access for fire inspection and maintain first aid/fire extinguishers per the Safety and Health at Work Act. No structural load inspection applies for a standard office lease.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Department of Taxation, Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Cyprus; principal e-portal is the 'Ariadne' Tax Information System (TIS) at taxportal.mof.gov.cy. Corporate incorporation (HE77 Private Limited Company) is administered by the Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRCOR) via efiling.drcor.mcit.gov.cy. VAT administration sits within the same Department of Taxation (Nicosia HQ).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the HE77 Private Limited Company at DRCOR and obtain the HE registration number. Step 2: Within 60 days of incorporation, file the Tax Department registration application (TD2001) through Ariadne/TIS to obtain the eight-digit Tax Identification Code (TIC/TIN) and open the corporate tax file, which governs annual IR4 returns and employer PAYE filings. Step 3: File VAT Form 101 (Application for VAT Registration) electronically before commencing taxable activity where the €15,600 threshold will be exceeded, or immediately on starting intra-Community acquisitions/distance sales; the VAT registration number takes the format CY prefix plus eight or nine characters with check digit. Step 4: For foreign-owned structures, appoint a Cyprus tax-resident secretary and certified public accountant/auditor, and file the statutory auditor appointment form (HE30). Non-resident sellers without a Cyprus fixed establishment are not ordinarily required to obtain a local TIC unless they hold Cyprus real estate or elect the OSS scheme, in which case a Cyprus VAT/OSS registration is mandatory.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a Cyprus tax-resident Ltd (managed and controlled in Cyprus) is taxed on worldwide income at the uniform 12.5% corporate rate, with a participation exemption for qualifying dividend and capital gain income and no sub-national corporate tax. The unit is treated as a standalone taxable person for VAT and cannot be treated as a pass-through entity under domestic law.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Cyprus has no US-style check-the-box election; entity classification is statutory. Available elections include: (1) Notional Interest Deduction (NID) on new qualifying equity contributions at the ten-year government bond yield plus 50 basis points; (2) IP-Box regime election granting an effective 80/92.5% deemed deduction on qualifying software/patent income subject to the OECD nexus limitation; (3) group loss relief election (75% affiliation, Cyprus/EU/EEA resident); (4) VAT group registration election under the Cyprus VAT Law for closely linked persons; (5) Union and Non-Union One-Stop-Shop (OSS) scheme election for B2C electronically supplied services, shifting VAT compliance to destination Member States; and (6) election to claim capital allowances and R&D-enhanced deductions on SaaS platform development costs.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are cross-checked by the Tax Department against Cyprus Customs MRN records, bank remittance evidence and VIES declarations. Where the 0% rate is disallowed, VAT is assessed retroactively at 19%, plus statutory interest (currently 5% per annum) and additional tax of up to 10% for late or defective returns; deliberate misdeclaration or fabricated export documentation attracts civil penalties of up to 100% of the differential VAT and criminal prosecution with fines and imprisonment of up to five years for directors and officers. The default assessment window is six years, extended to ten years where fraud or wilful misstatement is proven. Refund claims are suspended in whole or part pending audit clearance by the Tax Commissioner.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Cyprus (Κεντρική Τράπεζα της Κύπρου), operating within the European System of Central Banks and the ECB Single Supervisory Mechanism for credit institutions; the CBC supervises licensed banks, monitors balance-of-payments statistical reporting, and enforces EU anti-money laundering directives through its AML Directive issued under the Prevention and Suppression of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Law (L.188(I)/2007, as amended).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full current-account and capital-account convertibility. Cyprus has been an EU member since 2004 and adopted the euro in 2008; therefore there is no FX licensing, no prior-exchange-control approval, and no central bank permission requirement for currency conversion or cross-border transfers. Profit remittance is unrestricted: dividends paid by a Cyprus LTD to non-resident shareholders are exempt from Cypriot withholding tax, and dividends to EU/EEA parent companies are protected under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive. All residual crisis-era capital controls imposed in 2013 were fully lifted by 2016 and no standby restrictions remain. The only residual obligation is statistical: banks report cross-border flows to the CBC under its International Transactions Reporting System (ITRS), and transfers above EUR 10,000 in cash are subject to the EU cash control regulation (EU) 2018/1672. Convertibility is therefore de jure and de facto unrestricted for a standard low-risk PropTech SaaS treasury.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Cyprus imposes no statutory surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion into EUR, and no time limit for repatriating or holding export proceeds. A Cyprus LTD may retain USD, EUR, GBP, or multi-currency operating balances in CBC-licensed banks without any FX conversion obligation. The only compliance duties are indirect: export receivables must be recorded in the audited financial statements for the 12.5% corporate income tax calculation, and transfer pricing documentation must support intra-group international service flows.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Cyprus Public Company Ltd
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (multi-currency EUR/USD/GBP) and Capital Escrow Account for investor funds
Operational Account (EUR and USD) and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: MEDIUM-HIGH as a supplementary rail, LOW-HIGH as a primary settlement rail. EEA-licensed and passported Electronic Money Institutions (PSD2-authorized, e.g., Wise, MangoPay or CBC-licensed EMIs) may be used for low-value cross-border disbursements, Stripe payout concentration, and US ACH receipts, but the primary treasury and statutory settlement accounts must be held with a CBC-licensed credit institution to satisfy AML supervision, corporate banking covenants, and Cyprus tax residency evidence. Pure offshore/non-EEA digital EMIs without a correspondent banking relationship will be rejected by Cypriot banks in account relationships, and crypto-denominated rails or stablecoin settlement are not permissible for operating or escrow flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No blanket statutory mandate requires physical attendance. The CBC AML Directive permits remote on-boarding via live video identification where the bank can achieve an equivalent level of assurance. In practical application for a Low_Risk_Standard PropTech SaaS entity, at least one director or the UBO must attend a live interview call with the bank compliance officer; the Cyprus registered agent (secretary/auditor) may substitute a certified KYC pack for other signatories, and physical branch presence may be waived entirely for non-signatory shareholders. Banks retain the right to require an in-branch or in-country meeting if adverse media is identified, if the UBO is resident in a non-EEA high-risk jurisdiction, or if the capital injection exceeds materially the stated business plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity — ultimate beneficial ownership obscured through nominee shareholders, intermediate holding chains, or unregistered trust structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified extract from the Cyprus Registrar of Companies; UBO declaration filed under the Cyprus Beneficial Ownership Register framework; an unambiguous corporate structure chart covering every intermediate entity to the natural person; certified passport copies of the UBO; and a signed source-of-wealth statement with corroborating evidence (historical tax returns, sale-of-shares contracts, liquidation distributions, or bank reference letters).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure — UBO, shareholders, or material counterparties connected to US, EU, UN, or UK sanctions lists, or to jurisdictions with negative AML/CFT reputational standing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed sanctions/PEP questionnaires for all directors and UBOs; automated OFAC/EU/UN consolidated list screening results; current tax residence certificates (for Cyprus: T.D. 101 or equivalent); bank reference letters from the UBO home bank covering at least three years; and a written board undertaking confirming that no sanctioned proceeds or designated persons will benefit from the treasury accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds mismatch — inbound share-capital injection disproportionate to the stated SaaS revenue model or early-stage financial statements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or management financial statements of the Cyprus entity; the shareholder's bank statements tracing the funds' origin; the corporate resolution authorizing capital increase and share allotment; certified copy of the share register/HE32 filing; and, where applicable, the investor's audited accounts or sale-and-purchase documentation proving accumulated legitimate earnings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment-flow red flags — collection model that could mask third-party funds (e.g., landlord/tenant deposits passing through the corporate account without a client-money framework).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed SaaS/PropTech business plan; standard customer subscription contracts with property managers/landlords; flow diagram of Stripe Billing and ACH Direct collection into the treasury accounts; a signed declaration stating that the platform does not accept cash or crypto and that any tenant deposits are held under a segregated client-money ledger or third-party escrow; and evidence of the chargeback and refund policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Statutory registry non-compliance — gaps in annual filings, unreported director/UBO changes, or inactive registry status of the Cyprus entity or its parent.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Up-to-date company search from the Registrar of Companies; certified copies of all HE32 annual returns and acts-in-procedure filings; a complete minutes-and-resolutions book; the registered agent's certificate confirming continuous good standing; and a legal opinion from a Cyprus licensed law firm confirming the entity is duly incorporated, tax-resident, and compliant with Companies Law Cap. 113.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections flow through TARGET2/SEPA for EUR transfers and the SWIFT correspondent network for non-EUR. For equity injection: SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's bank to the Cyprus entity's EUR account with field 70 clearly stating 'SHARE CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION — CY_LTD — board resolution dated DD/MM/YYYY'. SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) may be used where the shareholder is in the EEA and the EUR amount is within SEPA limits; USD or GBP injections require MT103. The CBC/EU balance-of-payments statistical framework requires the bank to classify the transaction under the BPM6 direct investment equity category (the ECB '5D' code) or shareholder loan category ('5E') for related-party debt. The bank will request: (i) certified board resolution authorizing the increase or call of share capital; (ii) updated share register and share certificates; (iii) UBO declaration and source-of-funds proof; (iv) if the injection exceeds USD 100,000 or originates outside the EEA, the full evidentiary defense dossier; and (v) confirmation that no cash above EUR 10,000 is used, per EU cash control rules. No CBC license, FX approval, or convertibility permit is required at either inbound or outbound stage.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The base clearing rail is SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT/instant SEPA) for all EUR disbursements inside the EEA, covering vendor payments, payroll, cloud infrastructure, and Irish/Polish tech subcontractors at zero FX cost. For non-EEA and non-EUR payments (e.g., US cloud providers, international marketing agencies, USD-denominated debt service), the rail is SWIFT MT103 with standard debtor/beneficiary information and invoice references. Commercial Documentary Credits (MT700 LC at sight or confirmed) are permissible for high-value physical-asset or licensed-software acquisitions, but the low-indentity SaaS model defaults to open-account MT103 transfers supported by supplier invoices. US-side subscription receipts from Stripe Billing and ACH Direct may be aggregated through a US partner bank or authorized EMI and periodically swept to the Cyprus EUR account, using a USD account held at the Cypriot bank to reduce conversion slippage. All outbound flows above bank-specific thresholds are captured by the CBC's International Transactions Reporting System; the corporate client should submit an annual anticipated payment schedule so the bank can assign correct balance-of-payments statistical codes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD Outright Forward (delivery-based) — executed with the on-boarding Cypriot bank under ISDA 2002 or European master agreement; suitable for hedging USD-denominated SaaS revenue into EUR; typical minimum notional EUR 250,000 for a corporate relationship.

FX Swap (spot-forward or tom-next) — available through the bank treasury desk for short-dated liquidity matching between USD inbound receipts and EUR operating costs; recorded under CBC statistical reporting and not subject to any convertibility restriction.

FX Option (plain vanilla or barrier) — permitted to protect a defined USD/EUR budget rate while retaining upside from favorable conversion; requires ISDA/CSA master agreement with margin posting consistent with the bank's credit policy.

Cross-Currency Swap — appropriate for longer-dated, USD-denominated venture debt or intra-group loan exposures where principal and interest are USD and operating revenues are EUR; requires a formal board-approved FX risk policy.

Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) — permissible only for residual emerging-market exposures such as CNY, KRW, INR, or other restricted-convertibility currencies where the Cypriot bank's global desk provides synthetic deliverability; EUR/USD NDF is neither available nor required because EUR/USD is fully convertible. Any NDF usage requires explicit board sign-off, confirmed economic substance, and documented hedge accounting treatment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (RoC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 42 days after the company's annual general meeting; for calendar-year aligned private limited companies the RoC administrative deadline is conventionally 30 June following the annual return date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default fine of up to EUR 500 per company and per officer; repeated or continued default can trigger administrative strike-off under section 327 of the Cyprus Companies Law, Cap. 113.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (RoC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable by 30 June of each calendar year for every registered Cyprus private limited company.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of EUR 50 if paid between 1 July and 30 September; late fee increases to EUR 75 from 1 October onward; unpaid annual levy for more than eight months may lead to strike-off and dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Annual Financial Statements and Directors' Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (RoC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be filed within 12 months from the end of the company's financial year; for a 31 December year-end this means no later than 31 December of the following calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties and potential daily default fines under Companies Law; prolonged failure to deliver audited accounts to the RoC is grounds for Registrar-initiated strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Form TD4) with Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar tax year, Form TD4 is due by 31 March of the following year; provisional tax installments are generally due on 31 July and 31 December of the tax year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty up to EUR 100; interest and surcharges accrue on unpaid corporate tax, and persistent default can lead to mandatory assessment, recovery enforcement, and administrative fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO Annual Confirmation and Beneficial Ownership Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation due by 31 December of each year; updates to beneficial ownership details must also be filed within 30 days of any shareholding change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance is a criminal offense subject to fines up to EUR 20,000 and imprisonment officers; continuing default may attract additional daily penalty and administrative strike-off action.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Cyprus private limited company must appoint an auditor and undergo a statutory audit unless it qualifies for the small-company audit exemption under Cyprus Companies Law, Cap. 113. The exemption is available for small companies meeting low-turnover and small-balance-sheet criteria, generally turnover not exceeding EUR 50,000 and balance sheet total not exceeding EUR 100,000, provided no shareholder holding 10% or more of the issued shares requests an audit. Public-interest entities, group parents, and companies exceeding the applicable exemption thresholds are compulsorily audited.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared in accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted by the European Union; qualifying small companies may apply IFRS for SMEs. Cyprus does not retain a separate local Generally Accepted Accounting Practice for standard corporate statutory reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain an internal register of beneficial owners at its registered office and file beneficial ownership particulars with the RoC UBO Registry within 30 days of incorporation or any relevant change. Annually, no later than 31 December, an online confirmation of current beneficial ownership must be submitted through the Registrar's portal; any transfer of shares during the year must be reflected in both the register of members and the UBO confirmation.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Cyprus has no general tax holiday. The 12.5% standard CIT can be reduced by the IP Box regime (80% of qualifying intangible profits deductible, effective 2.5% rate), the Notional Interest Deduction on new equity, capital allowances, group relief, and foreign tax credits. A Cyprus-resident PropTech/real-estate SaaS company should document actual R&D and software exploitation to support IP Box claims.
